news.title: Why Falling Oil Prices Won't Save America From Inflation
news.summary: Don’t look to falling oil prices to stave off inflation now. Brent is down from above $100 to the low $90s; Saudi Arabia pumped 10.56 million barrels a day in October, back at pre-war levels and above its quota, and gasoline just posted its steepest one-day drop in 18 years. Consumer prices still rose an estimated 4% from a year earlier in October, with pump prices slightly lower, up from 3.7% in September, and core prices rose 0.3% in a single month. Expect the Fed to hike in December, but markets have already priced this in. October’s…

analysis.summary: Brent has fallen to the low $90s as Saudi Arabia pumps above quota at 10.56 mb/d, gasoline drops sharply, and an expected December Fed hike looms.
analysis.rationale: Above-quota Saudi production, falling refined product prices, and anticipated monetary tightening signal downward pressure on crude prices.
